title: Learner program cost bound
statement: Let $n,k$ be natural numbers, let $f:\{−1,1\}^n\to\{−1,1\}$ be a Boolean function, and let $\delta\in\mathbb{Q}$ satisfy $0<\delta\le 1/2$. For every outcome in the support of the learner's run on $f$, the number of random examples is at most $T_k R(n,k,\delta/T_k)$, the number of membership queries is zero, and the local work is at most $T_k W(n,k,\delta/T_k)$, where $T_0=1$, $T_{j+1}=1+2T_j$, and $R(n,k,q)$ and $W(n,k,q)$ are respectively the learner's uniform per-node random-example and local-work bounds at parameters $n,k,q$.
hypotheses_covered: Boolean target function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube
Outcome belongs to the support of the learner's run on the target
caveat: The formal statement uses specific uniform node-bound functions whose full definitions are not included in the supplied definitions list; the prose identifies their roles but does not expand their formulas.
